claim: For every integer \(n\ge4\), if \(\operatorname{occ}_{1122}(\pi)\) counts indices \(1\le i\le n-3\) in the canonical sequential form \(\pi\) of a non-crossing partition of \([n]\) with \(\pi_i=\pi_{i+1}<\pi_{i+2}=\pi_{i+3}\), then \(\sum_{\pi\in NC_n}\operatorname{occ}_{1122}(\pi)=\binom{2n-5}{n-4}\). For a uniformly random \(\Pi\in NC_n\), the mean is \(\frac{n(n+1)(n-3)}{8(2n-1)(2n-3)}\sim n/32\); for \(n<4\), the total is zero.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity: The theorem gives the total occurrence count and its mean, not the full distribution, variance, or a limit law.
The coefficient sequence is the known OEIS A002054 sequence shifted by three; the sequence itself is not claimed as new.
Finite enumeration through n=10 is a sanity check only; the all-size claim is proved by generating functions.
The originality assessment concerns this occurrence-statistic interpretation in canonical non-crossing partitions; an unindexed prior treatment remains a residual risk.
title: Total occurrences of the subword \(1122\) in non-crossing partitions
